maria_ng: Quick one: fresh venv on Windows + Python 3.11.3, following the Python quickstart. Async SDK call fails with SSL cert verify error inside httpcore. Sync client works. Anyone seen this?

alex_k: Hmm, corp MITM or missing CA in certifi bundle usually. Can you paste exact error and versions?

maria_ng: Error: `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate`. httpx 0.24.0, httpcore 0.16.0, anyio 3.6.2. certifi is installed and certifi.where() points to venv cacert.pem.

sam_w: Two suspicions: 1) Windows asyncio event loop (Proactor) interacts badly with winssl when passing a custom bundle. 2) httpcore may be using different TLS backend for async path. Can you share minimal async snippet?

maria_ng: Snippet:
```python
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncRedwoodClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key="x", verify=r"C:\\temp\\combined.pem")
    await c.generate("hello")

asyncio.run(main())
```
The same combined bundle works for curl and requests.

gina_ops: On Windows Python typically uses certifi file; system store isn't auto-injected. Setting SSL_CERT_FILE env var to your combined bundle often forces consistency. Also pyinstaller note: certifi data can be omitted when bundling.

alex_k: Good callouts. We currently forward `verify=` to httpx but docs don't show Windows guidance. Filing GH issue to track: async TLS verify on Windows + doc + typing stubs for Async client.

devex-bot: Created issue GH #3246: "Windows async TLS verify + Async typing stubs" https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/3246 :robot_face:

maria_ng: FYI, switching to alpha SDK and downgrading httpcore fixed it locally. I'll add repro steps to the issue. Also mypy flags missing overloads for Async client methods; a short typing note in quickstart would help.

alex_k: I'll add a Windows troubleshooting fragment to the quickstart and a typing note. We'll look into stubs next. Thanks!
